evidence: Receiving DO2 online sensor at t=48.0 h: 1.69 mg/L, first breach of the 2 mg/L hard limit (row available_at 48.0)
Receiving DO2 values t=48.0-52.0 h in range 1.10-1.69 mg/L, e.g., 1.15 mg/L at t=52 h — sustained violation under KEEP
Sharp DO drop from ~10.5 mg/L (t=47.8 h) to ~1.7 mg/L (t=48.0 h) indicates onset of high oxygen demand at decision time
Delayed assay P = 0.97 g/L at t=35.8 h and 2.69 g/L at t=47.9 h — active product formation argues against stop
allowed_actions: combined = [0.8 feed, 1.15 air], reduce_feed = [0.8, 1.0], increase_air = [1.0, 1.15], strong_feed_reduction = [0.6, 1.15]
submission.rationale: Receiving DO is in sustained violation of the 2 mg/L hard limit (1.1-1.69 mg/L at t=48-52 h), so KEEP is infeasible. Product is actively accumulating (P ~2.69 g/L and rising), so stop is unnecessary and would zero production. Combined action (feed x0.8, air x1.15) applies both demand reduction and supply increase: the observed DO plateau near 1.1-1.5 mg/L suggests oxygen demand is near balance with transfer, and a 20% demand cut plus 15% supply increase is the smallest bounded intervention predicted to restore DO >= 2 mg/L. It retains more product than strong_feed_reduction (feed x0.6), which is held as a fallback if the constraint is not met. increase_air alone (x1.15) is too marginal against a demand that drove an 85% DO drop.
submission.uncertainty: Hidden kinetic parameters and the true OUR/OTR balance are unavailable and no calibrated physics tool output was used, so the margin above 2 mg/L under combined cannot be quantified. If the demand surge resumes (as at ~48 h), combined may be insufficient; fallback would be strong_feed_reduction (feed x0.6) with air x1.15, or stop if no feasible plan is supported. Assay delay (20 h) limits product-state visibility; the last P value is 4 h stale.

evidence: Receiving online DO2 sensor: continuous decline from ~14.8 mg/L (t=0.2h) to ~10.5 mg/L (t=239h), then abrupt collapse to 1.2–1.7 mg/L for every sample t=240–259h, i.e., below the 2 mg/L hard limit for ~20 h already
Forward model reduce_feed: min DO 0.66 mg/L, 13h below limit, 0/5 feasible members
Forward model increase_air: min DO 0.70 mg/L, 13h below limit, 0/5 feasible members
Forward model combined: min DO 0.76 mg/L, 13h below limit, 0/5 feasible members
Forward model strong_feed_reduction (0.6 feed, 1.15 air): min DO 0.86 mg/L, 10h below limit, 0/5 feasible members
submission.rationale: The receiving fermentation has already violated the DO>=2 mg/L hard constraint: online sensor DO2 collapsed at ~240h from ~10.5 to ~1.2–1.7 mg/L and remains below 2.0 through the last observation (t=259h). Product assays show slow accumulation (2.69 g/L at 239h), so the batch carries real mass, but the constraint dominates. I evaluated all bounded interventions with the source-calibrated forward model: reduce_feed (min post-decision DO 0.66 mg/L, 13h below limit), increase_air (0.70, 13h), combined (0.76, 13h), and the strongest available, strong_feed_reduction at 0.6 feed/1.15 air (0.86, 10h below limit). Every action's central prediction stays far below 2 mg/L, and every sensitivity member (0/5 feasible in each case) also violates the limit. Per decision priority 2, a centrally infeasible plan cannot be justified by sensitivity members, which are not probabilities. Since no operating plan is supported as meeting the DO constraint, stop is the required decision, even though it forfeits the ~171 kg of counted product that continuing would nominally yield.
submission.uncertainty: The forward model is source-calibrated and imperfect (model mismatch with the receiving process possible; it already under-predicts vs. receiving observations in the crash window). However, the receiving process is currently measured at ~1.2–1.7 mg/L — well below the 2 mg/L limit even before any intervention — and no available action (max air multiplier 1.15, min feed 0.6) plausibly restores a >40% DO deficit given the model's consistent infeasibility across all sensitivity members. If true receiving dynamics were substantially more oxygen-favorable than the model, a mild combined action might recover, but no available evidence supports that; the observed sustained crash corroborates the model rather than contradicting it.
